The smallest square is at the upper-left, the middle square starts so that one of its corners is at the center of the smallest square, and the largest square starts so that one of its corners is at the center of the middle square. Visually, the smallest and middle squares overlap in the lower-right quadrant of the smallest square, the middle and largest squares overlap in the lower-right quadrant of the middle square, and the smallest and largest squares do not overlap. Reasoning: Use inclusion-exclusion. The side lengths are 2 cm, 4 cm, and 6 cm, so their individual areas are 2^2 = 4, 4^2 = 16, and 6^2 = 36, giving 56 cm^2 total before subtracting overlaps. Since the center of a square halves each side, the overlap between the 2 cm and 4 cm squares is 1 cm by 1 cm, area 1 cm^2. The overlap between the 4 cm and 6 cm squares is 2 cm by 2 cm, area 4 cm^2. There is no overlap between the first and third squares, so no triple-overlap correction is needed. Therefore the total area is 56 - 1 - 4 = 51 cm^2.

method.method_draft: Use inclusion-exclusion on the three squares. First read the image: the three squares are parallel, axis-aligned, and placed diagonally from upper-left to lower-right; the second square overlaps only the lower-right quadrant of the first, the third overlaps only the lower-right quadrant of the second, and the first and third do not overlap. From the text, take the side lengths as 2 cm, 4 cm, and 6 cm, with the relevant corner of each larger square placed at the center of the previous square. Since a center divides a square's side in half, the overlap of the 2 cm and 4 cm squares is a 1 cm by 1 cm square, area 1, and the overlap of the 4 cm and 6 cm squares is a 2 cm by 2 cm square, area 4. Add individual areas 2^2 + 4^2 + 6^2 = 56 and subtract the two overlaps: 56 - 1 - 4 = 51 cm^2.

method.method_draft: Build the union by adding only newly exposed area from largest to smallest. First read the image: the 6 cm square is the lower-right square, the 4 cm square extends up-left from it, and the 2 cm square extends up-left from the 4 cm square; all squares are parallel. Similarly, the 2 cm square has its center at the corner of the 4 cm square, so the covered part is one quadrant of the 2 cm square, 1 cm by 1 cm; it contributes 4 - 1 = 3 new square centimeters.
